subject: ventures/gbp-bulk-location-check
professional: a local-SEO specialist who runs Google Business Profile bulk uploads for multi-location clients, with a data-hygiene reviewer second: first checks are that column names and limits match Google's current bulk template and that format fixes (ZIP zeros, phone, hours) never change real data

evidence.correctness: Ran node probes against calc.mjs and recomputed outputs from sources I did not write: the 249-code country set is identical to tzdata's iso3166.tab (diff empty); ZIP leading-zero restore matches USPS 3-digit prefix allocation for MA, CT, NJ, NH, PR (and correctly refuses 3901/NH, a Maine prefix); phone checks agree with NANP and E.164 for 13 inputs; name length boundary 100/101 correct. One wrong result: Guam coordinates (144.75E) get a false 'positive longitude for a US location' warning. 8:00-5:00 is treated as overnight rather than a probable typo. The Google-specific rules cannot be recomputed offline (no outside source), which caps the score at 3.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features exercised: delimiter/UTF-16/BOM, column checks, store code duplicates and Excel damage, names, phones, URLs, hours, dates, country/state/postal, coordinates, labels, duplicate address, safe fixes, findings CSV, usage opt-out. sampleBrokenFile() yields 19 findings and repair() fixes the delimiter, hours separators and the CT ZIP; sampleFile() yields only an info line. No stubs or TODOs found. README test command works on Node 22.
evidence.verification: node --test ventures/gbp-bulk-location-check/*.test.mjs: 37 pass, 0 fail. Ten hand-seeded mutations in core logic: 5 caught (name length, lat/long zero, longitude bound, overnight hours, stuffing threshold) and 5 survived (E.164 max digits, NJ range, NH range, MA 055 range, hours closing limit). Boundaries in the data tables and phone limits are not pinned. Verification capped at 2.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (653 lines), index.html, usage.mjs, all tests. Pure functions, no DOM in the logic, tested separately, honest naming, UTF-16 handling, quoted-field parser with line numbers, grapheme-aware length via spread. Weaknesses: validate() is one very long function, unused locality argument, wide hand-maintained tables without citations, limits scattered as constants. Acceptable to a senior JS reviewer.
evidence.claims: Page, README and VENTURE.yaml state the tool reads rules 'from memory', has no Google template, lists what is not checked and carries the no-warranty, not-affiliated and local-only statements; the no-network claim is backed by page.test.mjs and my own grep. VENTURE.yaml hypothesis is marked untested. The live URL could not be loaded (HTTP 000 through the proxy, root also 000), so nothing about the served page is claimed beyond source. Source llms.txt/sitemap URL issues are source-only.
evidence.fitness: A marketing person with a bulk sheet can paste it, see line-numbered findings, and download a conservatively repaired file; the Excel-damage and delimiter fixes are real value. The job ends with an upload to Google, which this tool cannot confirm; the page says to upload two or three rows first. Unverified error-severity rules may send users to fix things Google accepts.
evidence.domain: A local-SEO/multi-location specialist (agency account manager who uploads GBP bulk sheets daily) would first check that the template columns, hours syntax and limits match Google's current bulk template and category list. The tool was built without access to it and cannot check category names, address validity or policy; its general format hygiene (E.164, ISO, ZIP) is sound, but the Google-specific parts are unverified, so 2.

checks.observed: HTTP 000 (proxy blocked; the host also failed on the site root), served page not verified; llms.txt in source links duncan-haywood.github.io, which the deploy rewrites (source-only)

mutations.change: overnight test b < a && b !== 0 -> b < a

defects.what: The ZIP-restoration table and the phone/hours limits are barely pinned by tests: 5 of 10 seeded changes left all 37 tests green (E.164 max 15->16, NJ range, NH range, MA 055 range, hours 24->25). The leading-zero restore is the product's headline fix and only MA/CT/sample-file cases are asserted.

latlong-sign warns 'Longitude is positive for a US location' for Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands (country US, state GU/MP), whose longitudes are correctly +144 to +146. A false warning on valid data from a territory whose ZIPs (969xx) the tool otherwise treats as US.

Every column name, limit (100, 80, 750, 64, 10 labels, 9 categories) and format (x for closed, 'Opening date' YYYY-MM-DD, special hours) is 'read from memory' and no Google template or help page was checked; the headline 'errors' (error severity) are therefore unverified rules a user may act on. Disclosed on the page, but severity is not downgraded and VENTURE.yaml hypotheses are untested.
8:00-5:00 (a 12-hour typo) is parsed as an overnight shift to 05:00 next day and only warned, and a 3-line 'Large file' limit of 10,000 rows is also from memory.
E.164 minimum of 8 digits flags valid short numbers (for example +683 4002, Niue, 7 digits) as an error.
nameFlags takes an unused locality parameter, and the ZIP+4 padding branch and ZERO_ZIP VT range include 055xx which is Massachusetts; validate() is one 300-line function.

llms.txt, sitemap.xml, robots.txt and the canonical link use github.io or relative URLs in source; the build rewrites these at deploy, so this is not a defect in what ships (served page could not be loaded to confirm).

verdict: A tidy, honest, local-only file checker whose generic hygiene checks (ISO country set identical to tzdata, USPS ZIP prefix restoration, NANP/E.164 phones, hours arithmetic) recompute correctly, with one false warning for Guam coordinates. It misses the bar on verification: 5 of 10 seeded mutations (E.164 max, NJ/NH/MA ZIP ranges, hours closing limit) leave all 37 tests green, and the Google-specific rules are admitted to be from memory, so domain is 2. The live page could not be loaded here (HTTP 000).
